crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Satellite Imagery
children.blurb: Satellite imagery as alternative data covers the use of overhead images to measure physical activity that shows up in economic or environmental indicators.

children.name: Card Transaction Data
children.blurb: Card transaction data covers aggregated and anonymized records of consumer purchases made with credit and debit cards, including point of sale, online, and mobile payments.

children.name: Sensor and Shipping Data
children.blurb: Sensor and shipping data covers the digital exhaust of physical movement: vessel positions from AIS, port call records, container and bulk cargo manifests where available, terminal gate and crane activity, truck and rail telematics, and fixed or mobile IoT sensors on assets and in facilities.

children.name: Mobile Location Data
children.blurb: Mobile location data is the record of where a phone or tablet has been, inferred from GPS, Wi-Fi, cell tower and beacon signals.

children.name: Web Data Collection
children.blurb: Web data collection is the practice of gathering information from public websites and web services for use as alternative data.

sections.body: Alternative data means information generated as a byproduct of ordinary activity rather than for analysis: satellite pictures of parking lots, card swipe records, ship transponder pings, phone location traces, and scraped web pages. In artificial intelligence work this data is fed into models that estimate things like retail foot traffic, crop yields, factory output, or port congestion before official statistics appear. The models are mostly computer vision for imagery and time series forecasting for the rest, with large language models increasingly used to parse messy text and filings. What makes the field distinctive is that the raw material is not collected for the question being asked, so cleaning and alignment matter as much as the modelling. The output is an estimate, not a measurement, and it usually carries a wide error band.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Satellite imagery is the most mature area, with commercial constellations producing frequent revisits and established methods for detecting objects and change, though cloud cover, resolution limits, and the cost of tasking still constrain what can be seen. Card transaction data is widely used but panel composition shifts over time, so panels must be reweighted and results validated against reported figures, and privacy rules in different jurisdictions limit how granular the data can be. Sensor and shipping feeds are reliable where hardware is standardised, less so where it is not, and location data has been repeatedly shown to be noisy and unrepresentative of whole populations. Web collection is technically easy and legally contested, with terms of service, robots conventions, and court rulings shaping what can be gathered and reused. The honest limit across all five is that correlation with a target does not establish causation, and backtests on alternative data are unusually prone to overfitting because the series are short and revised.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages follow the pipeline from physical observation to text. Satellite Imagery covers overhead sensing and the computer vision methods that turn pixels into counts of cars, ships, or hectares. Sensor and Shipping Data covers instrument readings and vessel or container tracking, the closest thing here to a continuous industrial feed. Card Transaction Data covers consumer spending signals and the panel construction and reweighting problems that come with them. Mobile Location Data covers device traces and the representativeness questions that make footfall estimates tricky. Web Data Collection covers scraping, crawling, and the legal and ethical boundaries around gathering public pages, and it is the page to read first if you want to understand where the other four get their text and metadata. Read together they show one workflow: acquire, clean, model, validate, and then decide how much to trust the number.
